# dsh-page-zoom
Page zoom for DeepSeek Harness / DSH Desktop.
Hold **Ctrl** and scroll the mouse wheel to scale the entire interface — sidebar, menus, settings, o
verlays and conversation alike. A magnifier glyph with the current percentage sits in the bottom-rig
d conversation alike. A magnifier glyph with the current percentage sits in the bottom-right corner.
English | 简体中文
## Controls
| Gesture | Result |

| `Ctrl` + mouse wheel up | Zoom in one step |
| `Ctrl` + mouse wheel down | Zoom out one step |

- Step: **5%** per wheel notch
- Range: **30% – 200%**
- The level is remembered (`localStorage`), s
o it survives a reload.
There are no buttons, no menus and no keyboard shortcuts — the readout is display-only.
## The readout

- Bottom-right corner, **12px / 10px** from the edges.
- **A magnifier glyph, then the number.** A b

are `100%` in a corner means nothing
on its own; the glyph is the convention browsers and phones alr

eady use for
this exact reading.
- Display only: `pointer-events: none`, so it never intercepts a cl

ick and never
gets in the way of the UI underneath.
- No box, no border, no background — it borrows

the app's own font stack
(`--dsw-font-family`) and its muted tertiary label colour
(`--dsw-alias-lab

el-tertiary`), so it reads as part of the chrome rather than
as a floating widget.
- **Scaled with t

he page, not against it.** The readout grows and shrinks with
everything else, and so does its gap f

rom the corner, so it stays proportional
to the app's own layout: 47×13 at 100%, 93×26 at 200%, 12×4

at 30%. Whatever it
does not cover at 100%, it does not cover at 200% either.

This works without any arithmetic because a fixed box's visual offset is the
declared value multipli

ed by its own `zoom` **and** by every ancestor `zoom`.
Keeping the element's zoom at 1 and the decla

red inset constant is therefore
already linear in the page zoom. Multiplying the value by the level

as well
makes it quadratic — a declared 24px renders as 48px at 200%.
- `role="img"` with an `aria-l

abel`, deliberately **not** `role="status"`.
`status` is a live region, so a screen reader would int

errupt with
"Page zoom 105%", "Page zoom 110%" on every wheel notch.

## How it works

Zoom is the CSS `zoom` property set on the document element, **not**
`transform: scale`. `zoom` refl

ows layout exactly like the browser's own zoom, so
fixed-position chrome keeps working. `transform`

would leave fixed elements
clipped and would additionally turn the root into a containing block for

every
`position: fixed` descendant.

DeepSeek Harness ships no page zoom of its own: the only typography setting is
`ui-theme.fontSize`,

which affects conversation body text only — sidebar labels,
menus and settings chrome are fixed pixe

l sizes. This plugin adds the missing
gesture.

The listener sits on `window` in the **bubble** phase with `{ passive: false }`,
and it yields to an

y surface that already claimed the event
(`event.defaultPrevented`). That ordering matters: the side

bar's document preview
binds its own cursor-anchored Ctrl+wheel zoom on its scrollport and calls
`pr

eventDefault()`. A capture-phase listener on `document` would fire before that
handler ever ran, and

`stopPropagation()` there would kill the preview's zoom
outright. Being last in line keeps the prev

iew working while every other surface
still falls through to page zoom. It also overrides the browse

r's native zoom
when the Harness is opened in a plain browser tab.

The whole thing is plain DOM — no React surface, no host-side code, no network
access, no storage be
yond one `localStorage` key.
